# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five in Volume 1, reaching around forty-nine by Volume 3  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c23 P11](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0011), [v2 c23 P13](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0013)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014), [v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014)</sub>; Mrs.

## Appearance

Rosalind Penrose is a tiny, attractive woman with snow-white, wavy, thick hair styled in flattering puffs and coils. She has an almost youthful face with rosy cheeks, dimples, and large, gentle wood-brown eyes containing flecks of gold. She dresses in delicate, youthful gowns such as cream muslin with light-colored roses or forget-me-not organdy, along with a gray silk shawl.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014), [v1 c27 P16](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0016), [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v2 c30 P3](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0003)_

## Personality

Rosalind possesses a bright, youthful, and imaginative disposition, enjoying playful pretense, fairy tales, and nature. Although she can be proud and moody at times, her nature is deeply affectionate, romantic, and charming. She prefers a quiet, secluded lifestyle over general society, though she thoroughly delights in the company of close friends.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and playful  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010)</sub>
- Proud and moody  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

## Abilities

- Talented at garden cultivation and plant care  <sub>[v2 c13 P50](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0050)</sub>
- Skilled in creating a charming, hospitable home atmosphere

## Goals

- To live peacefully amidst nature and imaginations in her stone cottage  <sub>[v2 c13 P45](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0045)</sub>
- To be reunited in love with Stephen Stanhope  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c28 P59](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0059)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose resided at Echo Cottage in Welby, living a quiet and imaginative life accompanied by her hired girl, Belinda the Fourth. Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke visited her to inquire about directions, resulting in an immediate friendship and a festive tea party. Following an accidental leap onto Rosalind's bed during a night visit, Nell apologized directly to Rosalind, who forgave her and invited her for regular chats. During the winter, Rosalind offered to host Nell for a week during her school break. Later, when Nell brought Stephen Stanhope's son, Cedric, to visit, Rosalind felt a deep affection for the boy due to his resemblance to his father. Eventually, Nell informed Rosalind that Stephen wished to visit her. Stephen arrived at Echo Cottage, where the long-separated lovers reconciled, resulting in their marriage late the following summer in the cottage garden. After the wedding, Rosalind departed with her husband for Boston and a journey to the Pacific coast, planning to return to Echo Cottage for future summers.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014), [v2 c23 P1](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0001), [v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027), [v2 c28 P38](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0038), [v2 c28 P59](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0059), [v2 c29 P11](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0011), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033)_

## Background by volume

- Born in East Welby to parents who named her Rosalind due to their love for lavender  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Raised in Echo Cottage, a sandstone home built by her father eighty years prior  <sub>[v1 c26 P14](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0014)</sub>
- Engaged in her youth to Stephen Stanhope before a foolish quarrel broke their betrothal  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c23 P16](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0016), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Lived as a recluse at Echo Cottage for years accompanied only by a young hired girl named Belinda  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> Pride together with moodiness form a terrible mixture, Nell. However, I could never feel affection for anyone else, nor did I desire to.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> A fractured heart in actual life is not nearly as terrible as it appears in novels.
